# Dashboard page — M3 guidance

<!-- Generated by apps/site/scripts/one-off/migrate-guidance.mjs. Do not edit by hand.
     The component pages carry the reference; this file carries the guidance. -->

## Web

### Features

Reach for the dashboard page when the screen is an overview: stat cards, activity rows and an ops queue composed into one page. `stats` are data — id, label, value, delta, tone, icon, description, link — rendered as a link-card grid, `activityRows` ride the two-line list with row press, and `queueTable` passes straight through to the data table. The passthrough is the point: columns, rows, sort, page and selection stay host-owned through it, and the template adds no table state of its own. There is no charting — stats are cards with values and deltas, and visualisation is the host's — and no fetching: everything arrives as props while `loading` only paints the skeleton. The three regions are labelled sections under `statsLabel`, `activityLabel` and `queueLabel`, stat deltas are host status pills so movement reads through the tone registry, and `children` slots extra display sections like charts around them.

## Native

### Features

Reach for the dashboard page when the screen is an overview: stat cards, activity rows and an ops queue composed into one page — the native twin under the same contract. `stats` are data — id, label, value, delta, tone, icon and description — rendered as cards activating through select with the stat id, since there are no link rows on this renderer, while `activityRows` ride the two-line list with row press and `queueTable` passes straight through to the data table. The passthrough is the point: columns, rows, sort, page and selection stay host-owned through it, and the template adds no table state of its own. There is no charting and no fetching — everything arrives as props while `loading` renders the skeleton list — and the three regions are labelled sections, so the page announces as regions rather than one long run.
